cells.tense: Right now the fire is lit and the adjusting is the work itself.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take the thing you're genuinely excited about and strip it to its sharpest reason. Act on it that same day, even if the whole plan is still soft.
cells.core:
You can hold a direction loosely and keep it moving at the same time. Where you're balancing, you read the pace around you and add or take away without announcing it, and the confidence you carry isn't performed — it's just what's left when the adjusting is working. The plan is allowed to be unfinished. The momentum is real.

What this balance is free to feed next is precision. Take what you're most excited about and cut it down to its sharpest reason — the logic under the enthusiasm, not the enthusiasm itself. Then act on that reason the same day, while the fire's still warm. You don't have to settle the whole plan. Just that one clean cut, and whatever follows it.
cells.sheetLine: You can keep the fire lit and find the sharp edge too.
cells.verb: lighting the fire before knowing where it leads
cells.place: where you keep adding and taking away to hold the flow steady

cells.tense: Soon the fire will be running ahead, and the adjusting will become forcing it.
cells.act: ask the question you do not know the answer to
cells.ask: When you notice yourself pushing a plan past its own timing, ask a question you don't know the answer to. Sit with it a day before acting.
cells.core:
The confidence that usually draws people in is starting to pull ahead of what's actually ready. You read the room and adjust, but the adjusting has turned into steering, and the steering has turned into pushing a timeline that isn't yours to push. The spark is still bright. It's just running out in front of the thing it's supposed to be lighting.

Stepping back here takes a question, not a plan. Ask something real — something you don't already know — and let not knowing be where you stand for a day. The fire can wait that long. Whatever you find in the waiting is the thing the pushing was trying to get to anyway.

cells.tense: The fire was lit back there, and you're still standing near the door it came through.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Give ten minutes to something you already keep alive — a plant, a corner of the kitchen, a habit — and do whatever it needs, nothing extra.
cells.core:
The door is behind you now and part of you hasn't moved through it. Where you balance, the old pace is still running — you're reading a room you're no longer in, adjusting for a rhythm that moved on. The spark isn't gone. It's just sitting down, waiting for the version of you that already walked through to come back and pick it up.

What recharges this is not more fire. It's attending to something small with fresh hands — the way you'd learn a plant by caring for it, not by planning how it grows. Ten minutes, one living thing, whatever it actually needs. Care doesn't exhaust when it's this small. And tending something that lives in the present is what walks you back into the room you're already standing in.
cells.sheetLine: The fire's still lit. You're at a door you already walked through.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but the writing is still being done in the room.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Set down the next solid move you can see, as if you meant it. Nothing before it, nothing after it. Let it stand and keep standing.
cells.core:
You're already adjusting the flow, already lighting small fires, already drawing people forward — and by your own account you were just going along with it. The confidence is doing its work. The name on it has gone missing. You file the steering under circumstance and the spark under luck, and the room keeps moving.

What comes back first is the simplest form of the same thing: a single solid move. Not the vision, not the strategy — the next thing you can see clearly, laid down like a builder lays stone. It doesn't need an audience or an explanation. Making the move shows you it was yours. The move holds whether or not you take credit, and taking credit gets easier each time you feel it hold.
